summary: Verified frontend fix for the Video Endpoint preview modal iframe-overflow bug. Route path is /:mainSiteSlug/video-endpoints (found at /app/frontend/src/App.js:291), so tested via /grk/video-endpoints after logging in as admkoodh@koodh.com. DB had zero video_endpoints, so seeded two TEST_ rows into the video_endpoints collection under the GRK main site (cd60a9fb-…): (1) 'Vimeo GRK' with the EXACT embed_html from the review request (<iframe src=vimeo.com/event/2848605/embed width=100% height=450 ...>), and (2) 'TEST YouTube' with a hardcoded 560×315 embed. Both endpoints render inside the preview dialog with pixel-perfect containment: modal box = 768×687.9 at x=576; preview container = 718×403.9 at x=601 (16:9 exact — computed aspect-ratio 1.7777, matches 16/9 spec); iframe rect coincides with preview rect (718×403.875, position=absolute, inset:0px). Iframe right edge sits 25px INSIDE the modal right edge (25px padding = p-6, expected). body.scrollWidth == innerWidth == 1920 → no horizontal page overflow. The 'preview-embed-textarea' data-testid is present with correct copy button below. Regression: (a) 'New endpoint' dialog opens cleanly (video-name-input present, .clara-video-preview class does NOT leak in, dialog width 672px), (b) create dialog CSS unaffected by the .clara-video-preview scoped rules in App.css:349-359. Both YouTube (width=560 height=315) and Vimeo (width=100% height=450) hardcoded attributes are correctly overridden — position:absolute inset:0 width:100%!important height:100%!important applied. Seed data cleaned up after test (0 rows remain in video_endpoints).
critical_code_review_comments: VideoEndpointsPage.js:537-552 — Preview Dialog fix is textbook: DialogContent gets `max-w-3xl w-[92vw] overflow-hidden p-6` (viewport-safe cap + horizontal clipping), and the inner preview <div> is `relative w-full rounded-lg overflow-hidden bg-black clara-video-preview` with inline style `aspectRatio: '16 / 9'`. This creates a proper positioning context so the App.css absolute-fill rules take effect. Confirmed inspector output: computed aspectRatio='16 / 9', overflow='hidden', position='relative' — all as expected.

App.css:345-359 — Scoped `.clara-video-preview iframe/video/embed/object` selector correctly targets ANY media element pasted into the embed_html (iframe/video/embed/object) with `position:absolute; inset:0; width:100%!important; height:100%!important; border:0; display:block`. The !important is necessary because pasted YouTube/Vimeo snippets include inline width/height attributes. Confirmed via getComputedStyle: iframe position=absolute, width=718px height=403.875px (exactly matches container).
The class `clara-video-preview` scope is tight — verified it does NOT bleed into the create/edit Dialog (checked via querySelector('.clara-video-preview') === null when the create dialog is open).

Minor observation (not a bug in THIS fix): the empty state / no-endpoint state was reproducible because dev database was empty. Suggest adding a `LoadingSpinner` fallback OR at least surfacing the 500 backend error more clearly in the toast (currently just 'Failed to load video endpoints') — hard to diagnose without checking network. Not blocking for this iteration.

rca of the issue: N/A — reviewing fixed code. Original bug: `<iframe width="100%" height="450">` inside a `<div class='aspect-video w-full'>` — the 450px hardcoded height forced the iframe out of the aspect-video ratio box (which would want ~403px for a 718px-wide container), and the `w-full` parent didn't clip. Fix (verified working): (1) replaced `aspect-video` with an inline `aspectRatio: '16 / 9'` + `overflow-hidden` on the wrapper; (2) added scoped App.css rules that force ANY iframe/video/embed/object descendant to position:absolute inset:0 width/height:100% with !important; (3) hardened DialogContent with `w-[92vw] overflow-hidden p-6` so the modal itself never exceeds viewport. All three layers verified in-browser: iframe now exactly 718×403.875 (matches 16:9 container), 25px inside modal right edge (= p-6 padding), no page horizontal overflow.
